issue.title: Memory: 367.6 MB Floating point exception (core dumped)
issue.body:
### What happens?

Between `1.4.4` and `1.5.2` a script I use started failing with:

```
Memory: 367.6 MBFloating point exception (core dumped)
```

### To Reproduce

Can't post source DB, but it uses a `postgres_attach` and looks like this:

```sql

PRAGMA temp_directory='/tmp/dump-legacy.duck.db';
.print creating tables

CREATE TABLE table1 (...);
CREATE TABLE table2 (...);

.print connect to Postgres DB

INSTALL postgres;
LOAD postgres;

CALL postgres_attach(
    concat('host=', getenv('PGHOST'),
    ' dbname=', getenv('PGDATABASE'),
    ' user=',  getenv('PGUSER'),
    ' password=', getenv('PGPASSWORD'))
    );

.timer on

INSERT INTO table1 (...)
    SELECT  ... FROM "PostgresTable1";

INSERT INTO table2 (...)
    SELECT  ... FROM "PostgresTable2";
```

It successfully completes a few tables, then consistently fails on the same one.

### OS:

Ubuntu 20.04.4

### DuckDB Version:

1.5.2

### DuckDB Client:

CLI

### Hardware:

_No response_

### Full Name:

Dave Tapley

### Affiliation:

JE Fuller

### Did you include all relevant configuration (e.g., CPU architecture, Linux distribution) to reproduce the issue?

- [x] Yes, I have

### Did you include all code required to reproduce the issue?

- [ ] Yes, I have

### Did you include all relevant data sets for reproducing the issue?

No - I cannot share the data sets because they are confidential

comments.body: Hi, thanks for reporting!. We’ll need a minimal reproducible example to find the root cause of this. Please let us know if you’re able to provide one—even privately, if necessary.

Thanks for opening this issue in the DuckDB issue tracker! To resolve this issue, our team needs a reproducible example. This includes:

* A source code snippet which reproduces the issue.
* The snippet should be self-contained, i.e., it should contain all imports and should use relative paths instead of hard coded paths (please avoid `/Users/JohnDoe/...`).
* A lot of issues can be reproduced with plain SQL code executed in the [DuckDB command line client](https://duckdb.org/docs/api/cli/overview). If you can provide such an example, it greatly simplifies the reproduction process and likely results in a faster fix.
* If the script needs additional data, please share the data as a CSV, JSON, or Parquet file. Unfortunately, we cannot fix issues that can only be reproduced with a confidential data set. [Support contracts](https://duckdblabs.com/#support) allow sharing confidential data with the core DuckDB team under NDA.

For more detailed guidelines on how to create reproducible examples, please visit Stack Overflow's ["Minimal, Reproducible Example"](https://stackoverflow.com/help/minimal-reproducible-example) page.

I also encounter the same problem, but only with the progress bar enabled

Here is a script that I used to reproduce the crash (core dump) based on processing that triggers the progress bar

``` bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash                                                                                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
duckdb << EoS                                                                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
SET memory_limit = '1GB';                                                                                                                                                                                         
SET threads TO 1;                                                                                                                                                                                                 
--SET enable_progress_bar = false;                                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
CREATE TABLE a AS SELECT floor(random()*1000) AS j, floor(random()*10) AS x FROM generate_series(1,2000000);                                                                                                      
CREATE TABLE b AS SELECT floor(random()*1000) AS k, floor(random()*10) AS y FROM generate_series(1,2000000);                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
SELECT SUM(j+x) FROM a LEFT JOIN b ON j = k WHERE x >=5 and y <=5;                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
EoS 
```

here is the error that shows when launching the script
```
Memory: 142.4 MB./test_crash: line 14: 240378 Floating point exception   (core dumped) duckdb <<EoS
```

After removing the comment (`enable_progress_bar = false`), the problem disappear.

NB: depending on your computer, you might have to increase the series to 5, 8 or maybe 10 million (YMMV)

I think this should be fixed now in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/22836, where we made some changes related to the progress bar.

Could you please try again with the latest nightly build? You can find installation instructions here depending on your environment: https://duckdb.org/install/preview

> I think this should be fixed now in [#22836](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/22836), where we made some changes related to the progress bar.
> 
> Could you please try again with the latest nightly build? You can find installation instructions here depending on your environment: https://duckdb.org/install/preview

Indeed, the problem has been solved with the v1.5-dev.

Nevertheless, it persists with the v2.0-dev (tested with duckdb binary for the x86_64 architecture ; size = 64337736) which seems logic since PR #22836 only applies to the 1.5 branch.

Thanks

That is correct. The fix is currently only present in the `1.5` branch, which is the release branch for the next patch release, so it is expected to be available in `v1.5-dev` but not yet in `v2.0-dev`.  Bug fixes targeting patch releases are later synchronized with the branch that produces the next major release. As a result, the fix will be incorporated into `v2.0` once the relevant branch merges occur during the normal release cycle.
